digital-marketer.intro: Learn digital marketing from campaign planning to analytics. Reach customers where they actually spend time — WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Google — and prove what works with data.

skillDomains.name: Campaign Planning
skillDomains.description: Every campaign starts with a plan, not a post.

skills.name: Audience & Objective
skills.description: Define who you're reaching and what success looks like before spending a cent.

modules.title: Why campaigns fail
modules.content:
Most marketing campaigns fail for the same reason: no clear audience and no clear goal.

Compare:

  • Bad: "We want more customers."
  • Good: "We want 200 women aged 25–40 in Freetown to sign up for the WhatsApp ordering service by end of month."

The second one is specific enough to plan, execute, and measure. The first is a wish.

Every campaign needs

  1. Who — a specific group of people
  2. What — the exact action you want them to take
  3. When — a deadline
  4. How much — a budget

modules.title: Build a target audience
modules.content:
The four dimensions

  • Demographic — age, gender, income, location
  • Psychographic — values, interests, lifestyle
  • Behavioural — how they shop, what platforms they use
  • Pain — what problem are they trying to solve?

Example

"Young mothers in Accra aged 25–35, working professionals, who use Instagram daily and struggle to find time for grocery shopping."

When you can describe your customer this precisely, you know exactly which content to make and where to place it.

steps.q: Which is a well-formed campaign objective?
o: Get 150 sign-ups for the loyalty program by December 31 from customers in Nairobi
steps.f: Specific number, specific audience, specific deadline.

steps.q: You run a restaurant and want to fill tables on weeknights. Best campaign objective?
o: Get 40 weeknight reservations per week for 4 weeks
steps.f: Tie the objective directly to the business outcome.

steps.q: An objective like 'raise awareness' is weak because:
steps.f: If you can't measure it, you can't tell whether it worked.

modules.title: Write a campaign brief
modules.prompt: A small online fashion brand wants to sell 100 units of a new Ankara dress in 30 days. Write a one-paragraph campaign brief that covers: target audience, the specific action, budget, timeline, and how success will be measured.
modules.context: Real campaigns start with a written brief. This forces clarity before spending.

modules.title: Build a campaign brief template
modules.prompt: Design a one-page campaign brief template you would use for every client or internal campaign. It must be fillable in 15 minutes and cover every essential decision.
steps: Include sections for audience, objective, budget, timeline
Add a section for the key message
Add a section for which platforms
Add a section for how success is measured
Test it on a real or imagined campaign

skills.name: Content Strategy
skills.description: Plan what you'll publish, when, and why.

modules.title: The content types that work
modules.content:
By purpose

  • Attract — reels, tips, memes that reach new people
  • Engage — comments, polls, stories that keep current followers
  • Convert — product photos, testimonials, offers that drive sales

By format

  • Short video (reels, TikTok)
  • Static image (feed posts)
  • Story (ephemeral, casual)
  • Long-form (YouTube, blog)

A good content mix has all three purposes across all four formats.

modules.title: Build a content calendar
modules.content:
Posting randomly doesn't build an audience. Posting consistently does.

A simple calendar

  • Monday — motivational or educational
  • Wednesday — product or service showcase
  • Friday — behind-the-scenes or community
  • Daily stories — short, casual, real

Plan 2 weeks in advance. Batch-produce content in one session. This is how professionals stay consistent.

steps.q: You want to reach new people on Instagram. Best format?
steps.f: Reels reach new people. Feed photos mostly reach existing followers.

steps.q: You want to build trust with existing customers. Best format?
steps.f: Testimonials in stories feel personal and real.

steps.q: You have 4 hours to work on marketing this week. Best use?
steps.f: Batch production beats daily improvisation every time.

skillDomains.name: Paid Media
skillDomains.description: Spend money wisely. Ads work when targeting and creative are right.

skills.name: Meta Ads
skills.description: Ads on Facebook and Instagram — the biggest paid channel in West Africa.

modules.title: How Meta ads work
modules.content:
Meta ads (Facebook + Instagram) work on an auction system:

  1. You set a target audience, budget, and creative
  2. Facebook shows your ad to people in that audience
  3. You pay per impression or per click
  4. The algorithm optimises toward whatever goal you set

Campaign goals

  • Awareness — show the ad to many people cheaply
  • Traffic — send people to your site or WhatsApp
  • Engagement — get likes, comments, shares
  • Leads — get phone numbers or messages
  • Sales — convert directly

Choose the goal that matches what you actually want.

modules.title: Targeting on Meta
modules.content:
Three levels of targeting

  • Broad — age, gender, location. Cheapest, works best with strong creative.
  • Interest-based — people who follow certain pages or show certain behaviours.
  • Lookalike — Facebook finds people similar to your existing customers.

Best practice for small budgets

Start broad. Facebook's algorithm is smarter than your guesswork. Only narrow the audience if you have specific evidence you need to.

steps.q: You have 50,000 Le for a week of ads. Best approach?
o: Test 3 ads with 3 different creatives in one campaign
Wait until you have more money
steps.f: Test multiple creatives. Let data pick the winner, then put budget behind it.

steps.q: Your ad gets lots of views but no clicks. What's wrong?
steps.f: Views without clicks means the ad doesn't give a reason to act. Rework the creative.

steps.q: Your ad gets clicks but no sales. What do you check?
o: The landing page or WhatsApp response
steps.f: Clicks mean the ad works. Sales problems usually live on the destination.

modules.title: Build a real Meta campaign
modules.prompt: Design a Facebook/Instagram ad campaign for a real or imagined product. Include: 3 ad variations, the audience, the budget, the goal, and how you'd judge success after one week.
steps: Write 3 different ad copies and visual concepts
Define success: clicks, leads, or sales
Write a plan for what to do with the results

skillDomains.name: Analytics
skillDomains.description: Measure what matters. Guessing is expensive; measuring is free.

skills.name: Key Metrics
skills.description: Know the numbers that actually matter.

modules.title: The numbers that matter
modules.content:
Reach vs engagement

  • Reach — how many people saw your content
  • Engagement — likes, comments, shares, saves
  • Engagement rate — engagement ÷ reach × 100

Conversion

  • Click-through rate (CTR) — clicks ÷ impressions × 100
  • Conversion rate — sales ÷ visits × 100
  • Cost per acquisition (CPA) — ad spend ÷ sales

Revenue

  • Return on ad spend (ROAS) — revenue ÷ ad spend

A ROAS of 3 means every 1 Le spent returned 3 Le of revenue.

steps.q: You spent 20,000 Le on ads and made 80,000 Le in sales. What's the ROAS?
Your ad got 10,000 views and 100 clicks. What's the CTR?
steps.f: 100 ÷ 10,000 × 100 = 1%. A 1% CTR is a reasonable benchmark.

steps.q: You have a ROAS of 1.2. Are you making money?
o: Probably not — after product cost, you may be losing money
steps.f: A ROAS of 1.2 barely covers the ad spend. Add product cost and labour and you're often losing.

modules.title: Build a weekly analytics report
modules.prompt: Design a one-page weekly report for a small business. It should show the metrics that matter without overwhelming the reader.
steps: Choose 5-7 metrics that connect to business outcomes
Design a simple layout: this week vs last week
Add a short 'what this means' section
Add 2-3 recommended actions for the coming week
Test it on real data from any platform

skillDomains.name: Client Work
skillDomains.description: Turn marketing skill into income. Managing clients is a separate skill from running campaigns.

modules.title: What clients actually want
modules.content:
Clients don't buy marketing tactics. They buy outcomes. They want more sales, more customers, more awareness.

What they need from you

  • Clarity on what you'll do
  • A clear timeline
  • Regular, brief reports (not long ones)
  • Honest feedback when something isn't working
  • Predictable billing

The most common client complaints

  • "I don't know what you're doing"
  • "You didn't hit the deadline"
  • "The results are unclear"

Solve all three with a simple weekly update.

modules.title: Pitch a retainer
modules.prompt: A restaurant wants digital marketing. You'll do 12 posts per month, 2 ad campaigns, and weekly reporting. Describe how you'd structure the offer, what you'd charge, and how you'd set expectations.
modules.context: Retainers are the most stable income for a digital marketer.
